title: LEBER OPTIC ATROPHY AND DYSTONIA
alt_titles: LEBER HEREDITARY OPTIC NEUROPATHY WITH DYSTONIA
DYSTONIA, FAMILIAL, WITH VISUAL FAILURE AND STRIATAL LUCENCIES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by homoplasmic or heteroplasmic mutation in the mitochondrially encoded genes MT-ND6 (516006), MT-ND4 (516003), MT-ND1 (516000), or MT-ND3 (516002).

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by homoplasmic or heteroplasmic mutation in mitochondrially encoded genes.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3697G>A/ND1 mitochondrial DNA mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in the same family.
checks.explanation: The paper supports causation of LHON plus dystonia by an mtDNA mutation. It does not state whether mutations are homoplasmic or heteroplasmic, and it does not address the other genes.

checks.claim: LDYT can be caused by mutation in MT-ND6.
checks.evidence_quote: The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
checks.explanation: The abstract says that a mutation in ND6 has been suggested as the cause of LHON and/or dystonia.

checks.claim: LDYT can be caused by mutation in MT-ND4.
checks.evidence_quote: A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.
checks.explanation: An ND4 mutation was found in the family.

checks.claim: LDYT can be caused by mutation in MT-ND1.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3697G>A/ND1 mitochondrial DNA mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in the same family.
checks.explanation: The paper directly states that an ND1 mutation causes the LHON plus dystonia phenotype.

checks.claim: LDYT can be caused by mutation in MT-ND3.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.

paragraphs.text: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is a maternally inherited mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder. Affected people have vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia in different combinations (Wang et al., 2009). Within a family, some members have Leber optic neuropathy, some have dystonia, and some have both. The dystonia is associated with bilateral lesions of the striatum, especially the putamen (Marsden et al., 1986; Novotny et al., 1986).

checks.evidence_quote: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls LDYT a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder. It does not explicitly say 'maternally inherited', although it mentions affected individuals on the maternal side.

checks.evidence_quote: We studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease; 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration; and 1 had both disorders.
checks.explanation: The kindred included members with Leber disease alone, members with dystonia alone, and one member with both.

paragraphs.text: Jun et al. (1994) studied a 5-generation Hispanic family with LHON and/or early-onset dystonia. They identified a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 of the MT-ND6 gene, which changed a moderately conserved alanine to valine at residue 72 (A72V). All 6 maternal relatives tested, from 3 generations, carried the mutation. One woman with LHON was heteroplasmic. The authors gave 4 reasons for concluding that this was likely the disease-causing mutation: it was specific to the family, it altered a moderately conserved amino acid in a complex I gene, it was unique among haplogroup D mtDNAs, and it was heteroplasmic.

paragraphs.text: De Vries et al. (1996) studied a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia. The family had none of the mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON. Sequencing of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes found 2 changes: - a heteroplasmic A-to-G transition at nucleotide 11696 in the MT-ND4 gene, causing a val312-to-ile (V312I) substitution - a homoplasmic T-to-A change at nucleotide 14596 in the MT-ND6 gene, causing an ile26-to-met (I26M) substitution A muscle biopsy showed severe complex I deficiency. The authors suggested that this deficiency linked the mtDNA mutations to the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2009) studied a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients. Resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome found a m.10197G-A mutation in the MT-ND3 gene, causing an ala47-to-thr (A47T) substitution at a highly conserved residue. The mutation was on a haplogroup D4b background. It was homoplasmic in the leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. paragraphs.text: De Vries et al. (1996) studied a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia. Sequencing of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes found a heteroplasmic A-to-G transition at nucleotide 11696 in the MT-ND4 gene, causing a val312-to-ile (V312I) substitution. It occurred together with a homoplasmic 14596T-A mutation in MT-ND6. A muscle biopsy showed severe complex I deficiency, which the authors suggested linked the mtDNA mutations to the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Spruijt et al. (2007) studied a family with both LHON and spastic dystonia. The patient with LHON lacked the 3 primary LHON mutations. Screening of the complete mtDNA found a heteroplasmic 3697G-A mutation in the MT-ND1 gene, which seemed to be associated with an isolated complex I deficiency. The authors concluded that the mutation caused both LHON and spastic dystonia in the same family. They noted that this mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2009) studied a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients. Resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome found a m.10197G-A mutation in the MT-ND3 gene, causing an ala47-to-thr (A47T) substitution at a highly conserved residue. The mutation was on a haplogroup D4b background. It was homoplasmic in the leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. The authors noted that the same mutation had been reported in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.
